options: A Python class that looks up a Connection by conn_id and turns it into a real, usable connection object
A stored record of credentials in the Airflow UI
A type of task-level retry mechanism
A scheduling expression like a cron string
questions.explain: A Hook reads a Connection's fields and establishes an actual, working connection your code can use.

questions.q: In `hook.get_pandas_df("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders;")` using SnowflakeHook, what is actually happening?
options: Real SQL is being run against real Snowflake, using the connection the Hook resolved from a conn_id
The query is only validated, never executed
Airflow translates the SQL into a different language before running it
The Hook stores the query for later, manual execution
questions.explain: The Hook resolves the conn_id into an authenticated Snowflake session and runs the exact SQL you'd type in the Snowflake worksheet.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a Hook and an Operator?
options: A Hook is the low-level connection interface; an Operator is a higher-level, task-shaped wrapper (often built on a Hook)
They are two names for the exact same thing
A Hook can only be used once per DAG, while Operators can be reused
Operators cannot use Connections at all
questions.explain: Many Operators — like SnowflakeOperator — build a Hook internally and call its methods, so you don't have to write that code yourself.

questions.q: When would you reach for a Hook directly inside a PythonOperator instead of using an existing Operator?
options: When the logic is more than "run this SQL" — e.g. branching on a query result or pulling data into pandas for a transformation
Never — Hooks cannot be called from a PythonOperator
Only when there is no Connection configured
Whenever you want slower task execution
questions.explain: Hooks give you the raw connection so you can do arbitrary Python logic with it, beyond what a single-purpose Operator supports.

questions.q: True or false: SnowflakeOperator has nothing to do with SnowflakeHook — they are unrelated.
options: False — SnowflakeOperator builds a SnowflakeHook internally (from the conn_id) and calls its run method
True — Operators never use Hooks
True — Hooks are only used for network testing
False — but only because they share a name coincidentally
questions.explain: SnowflakeOperator is a thin wrapper: it gets a SnowflakeHook via get_db_hook() and calls hook.run(self.sql).
